newsitem.title: USA: Northeast Utilities sees year sales gains.
newsitem.headline: Northeast Utilities sees year sales gains.

text.p: Northeast Utilities is now projecting a 1.4 percent increase in retail power sales this year, the company's October 1996 "Financial Update" said.
It said the company's new sales forecast also projects increases of 0.7 percent next year and 1.6 percent in 1998.

On March 1, the utility filed with regulators projecting a 0.4 percent sales decline this year followed by a 1.1 percent gain in 1997 and a 2.0 percent increase in 1998, spokesman Jeffrey Kotkin said.
Despite cool weather in July, the Update said, the Northeast Utilities system continues to show unexpected sales strength.
Retail sales were up 2.4 percent over the first nine months of the year, 3.1 percent on a weather-adjusted basis.

It said residential sales were up 2.8 percent, commercial sales rose 3.2 percent and industrial sales were up 0.5 percent. One a weather-adjusted basis, residential and commercial sales were up 3.4 percent and 4.3 percent, respectively, it noted.
The Update also said Northeast Utilities report earnings after Tuesday's Board of Trustees meeting.
